fields.guideContent:
Fluid Adventures – Chichester Harbour & Hayling

Fluid Adventures offers guided canoe and kayak trips across several South Coast waterways. Choose the actual route first: the meeting point, duration and level of effort vary considerably.

Choosing a trip

The partner page lists Chichester Harbour outings, seal watching, sunset paddles and a Hayling Island circumnavigation among the wider range. The round-island option is described as an intermediate outing of around 13 miles and up to six hours. It should not be confused with a short introductory paddle.

Where to go

Departures vary by product, including Itchenor and Dell Quay for Chichester Harbour experiences. Use the meeting point on your booking confirmation, not the company’s general address. Build your day around the session time and allow space afterwards for changing and returning to your accommodation.

Facilities and suitability

The partner lists toilets and parking nearby, and says these canoe and kayak trips are not currently wheelchair accessible. Wear suitable layers, expect splashes and bring a change of clothing. Check age requirements and experience level for the exact trip. Weather and water conditions can change the arrangements, so read the operator’s instructions before setting off.

Cobnor Activities Centre

Cobnor Activities Centre is at Cobnor Point on the Chidham Peninsula. It is a mainland activity trip around Chichester Harbour, with bookable experiences on land and water.

What you can book

The partner page describes high ropes, keelboat sailing and paddlesport sessions, each booked as its own experience. Many sessions include instruction for beginners, while age and participation rules depend on the activity. Choose what your group actually wants to do before comparing dates.

Facilities and access

Listed facilities include parking, toilets, showers, outdoor seating and equipment for water-based activities. The centre can adapt some activities for individual needs; contact it about the specific session and any mobility requirements. Accessible facilities do not mean every water activity suits every participant.

Getting there and preparing

Use Cobnor Point, Chidham, PO18 8TE for the destination. The partner notes that nearby railway stations still require onward transport. Bring outdoor clothing and, for water activities, spare clothes and a towel. Use the booking options to choose an available session for your group.

fields.guideContent:
Chichester Harbour Water Tours

Chichester Harbour Water Tours gives you a seated way to enjoy the harbour, with guided scenic trips and wildlife-focused outings from Itchenor.

The experience

The partner lists harbour and bird-watching tours alongside seal-watching trips. Wildlife is part of the appeal, but sightings cannot be guaranteed. Choose the product that matches the time you have available and the interests of your group.

Boarding and facilities

Departures are from the public jetty at Itchenor. Walk to the waterside end, rather than waiting by the harbour office, and follow the instructions in your confirmation. The boat has passenger seating and safety equipment; the partner says you may bring drinks and snacks.

Accessibility and trip planning

The partner describes boarding through a door with assistance from the skipper. Contact the operator about wheelchair dimensions, tide-related access and your individual boarding needs before booking. Dress for exposed coastal weather even on a pleasant day. Allow time for parking and reaching the jetty, and check the sailing status before travelling from Hayling.

fields.guideContent:
Portsmouth Historic Dockyard

Portsmouth Historic Dockyard is a substantial day out in its own right. Ships, museums and naval stories give you far more to explore than a quick stop between other attractions.

What to see

The partner ticket lists major attractions including HMS Victory, HMS Warrior, HMS M.33, the Mary Rose Museum and Royal Navy museums. Check the precise ticket coverage and any restoration restrictions for your date. Some included sites are separate from the main waterfront entrance, so plan how you will reach them.

Tickets and revisiting

The advertised ticket offers repeat access for a year. Read the product terms to confirm activation, included sites and any exclusions. This can be useful if you are staying nearby and would prefer to spread the museums over more than one visit rather than rush them all in an afternoon.

Facilities and access

The partner lists cafés, toilets, accessible toilets, shops and parking nearby. Historic ships have uneven surfaces and confined areas, so consult the access information for the individual attractions. Assistance dogs are accepted; ordinary pets are not. Check companion-ticket arrangements when booking.

Make room for the day

The entrance is at Victory Gate in Portsmouth, close to Portsmouth Harbour station. It is a mainland outing from Hayling Island. Plan your return travel and leave time to sit down for food, especially with children or anyone who needs regular breaks.

Macdonald Botley Park Hotel & Spa

Macdonald Botley Park Hotel & Spa is in Boorley Green near Southampton. It belongs in the wider Hampshire options for a Hayling trip, with its own restaurant, spa and leisure club, rather than being described as a hotel on the island.

A hotel for a wider Hampshire break

The hotel has rooms and suites, meeting spaces and wedding facilities. It can make sense if your plans include Southampton or other Hampshire stops as well as Hayling. If your whole break revolves around the island’s beach and arcades, compare the extra driving with an on-island stay before choosing.

Food and leisure

The operator lists the Winchester Restaurant, Gallery Bar, Sports Bar and afternoon tea, alongside spa treatments and a leisure club with an 18-metre pool. Treatments and dining packages need checking against the chosen booking. A room-only rate and a spa break can include different things, even when the hotel is identical.

Arrival and accessibility

The published standard check-in is from 15:00 and check-out by 11:00; direct bookings may receive a later departure. The hotel advertises accessible rooms, so discuss the bedroom, bathroom and route to the facilities with reservations before booking. Its address is Winchester Road, Boorley Green, Southampton, SO32 2UA.

Choose the offer that matches your plans

Room stays, spa packages and park-and-cruise offers are grouped on this one hotel page. They are separate products with different inclusions. For a cruise package, confirm the departure port, transfer arrangements, parking duration and number of guests. For a spa break, check the treatment length and dining allowance. Keep the hotel choice and the package choice clear before paying.

fields.guideContent:
Village Hotel Portsmouth

Village Hotel Portsmouth is a modern mainland option on Lakeshore Drive. It suits a trip that combines Portsmouth with a separate visit to Hayling Island, especially if a gym, swimming pool and hotel restaurant matter to you.

What the hotel offers

The partner describes a 153-room hotel over five floors, with a lift and 24-hour reception. Its room photographs show a contemporary style, with different bedroom and bathroom arrangements. Match the room category to your booking: a gallery is useful for getting a feel for the property, but the selected room description is what establishes what you receive.

Leisure and food

An indoor pool, fitness facilities, sauna and steam room are listed, alongside a bar and restaurant. Check your rate for any leisure-access conditions and charges, and ask about children’s pool sessions if travelling as a family. Breakfast is available, but whether it is included depends on the rate. Free Wi-Fi is listed.

Parking, access and arrival

On-site parking is chargeable on the partner listing, which currently states £10 per vehicle per night. Confirm the amount for your stay. Check-in is from 15:00 and check-out by 11:00. Wheelchair access and restaurant access are listed, but contact the hotel about the bedroom and bathroom you actually need. The presence of a lift is useful information, not a substitute for checking the room layout.

Where it fits into your trip

This is Portsmouth accommodation, not an address on Hayling Island. Plan the journey to the island separately, and allow for the return drive after a beach or arcade visit. The Dockyard and Gunwharf Quays can form a Portsmouth day of their own. Use the booking button to see current availability, then compare the full price including parking, breakfast and any leisure extras.

fields.guideContent:
Sinah Warren Hotel

Sinah Warren is Warner’s adults-only coastal hotel on Ferry Road, overlooking Langstone Harbour. It is a different sort of stay from a family caravan park: the setting, evening entertainment and hotel leisure facilities are central to the break.

The setting and style of stay

The hotel sits on the south-west side of Hayling Island, with gardens and coastal views. Warner shows an indoor pool, an outdoor pool and lounge and dining spaces. Some rooms have a balcony or patio, but this depends on the room booked. The gallery shows the hotel setting and facilities, with photographs supplied by Warner.

Dining and entertainment

Warner promotes live entertainment as part of its breaks. Look at the programme for the dates you intend to travel; a tribute or themed event advertised for another weekend is not a promise about your stay. Check the board basis on the affiliate booking carefully, including breakfast and evening meals, rather than assuming it matches every package sold directly by Warner.

Planning a comfortable visit

The adults-only policy matters when choosing accommodation for a group. For mobility requirements, ask the hotel about the room’s location, bathroom, distances to the restaurant and entertainment areas, and access to leisure facilities. Specific accessible-room arrangements are more useful than a broad accessibility badge. Check the chosen rate for arrival and departure times, parking and any treatment charges.

Explore from the hotel

This is an on-island base for coastal time, with the option of a separate Portsmouth day. Keep enough space in the itinerary to enjoy the hotel itself if you are choosing it for leisure and evening entertainment. The booking button retains the existing ZenHotels affiliate option; it opens current availability and the terms for the particular room or package.

fields.guideContent:
Newtown House Hotel

Newtown House is an on-island hotel on Manor Road, handy for a break built around the beach and Hayling’s seaside attractions. The red-brick exterior and traditional lounge give it a different feel from a large modern chain hotel.

The hotel and its rooms

The partner listing describes 26 rooms across two floors. Its photographs show several bedroom styles, including twin rooms and four-poster beds, so use the room description for your chosen rate rather than assuming every room matches the main photograph. The hotel also has a garden and terrace. This is a place to use as a base for exploring the island, with somewhere to sit down at the end of the day.

Food, parking and everyday facilities

ZenHotels lists a bar, restaurant, breakfast, free Wi-Fi and free parking. Check whether breakfast is included in the room rate you select; a hotel offering breakfast does not mean every booking includes it. Laundry and luggage storage are also listed. For a short seaside break, being able to leave the car at the hotel and return for a meal is part of the appeal.

Accessibility and arrival

The listing reports wheelchair access to the restaurant and accessibility features, but also says there is no lift. Ask for confirmation of a suitable bedroom, bathroom and step-free route before booking if stairs would be a problem. The published check-in window is 15:00–23:00, with check-out by 10:30. Arrange a late arrival directly. The partner lists pets as not allowed; discuss assistance-dog arrangements with the hotel.

Making a Hayling break of it

Beachlands and Funland are the natural seaside pairing. Leave time for the beach or a quieter island walk rather than treating every day as a drive to Portsmouth. The wider attractions below are additional trips: Portsmouth and Chichester are not the same location as the hotel. The booking options give you a way to compare the actual room, board basis, cancellation terms and final total for your dates.

fields.guideContent:
The D-Day Story tickets

The D-Day Story in Southsea brings the planning and human experience of the Normandy landings into focus, with museum galleries and the surviving landing craft LCT 7074.

Inside the attraction

The listed ticket includes the museum galleries, landing craft, interactive displays, films and the Overlord Embroidery. It suits visitors who want to understand the people and decisions behind D-Day, rather than simply look at military vehicles.

Allow enough time

The partner suggests around one and a half to three hours, depending on how much you read and watch. Give the landing craft and galleries time of their own. This is a Southsea visit on the mainland; it can pair with a seafront walk without trying to squeeze the whole Dockyard into the same afternoon.

Facilities and tickets

The partner lists toilets, a café, shop, parking and a Changing Places facility. Check the attraction’s access information for any specific requirement, including the landing craft. Compare family ticket combinations against your group size and use the live booking page for available dates and the final price.

fields.guideContent:
Newtown House Hotel

Newtown House is an on-island hotel on Manor Road, handy for a break built around the beach and Hayling’s seaside attractions. The red-brick exterior and traditional lounge give it a different feel from a large modern chain hotel.

The hotel and its rooms

The partner listing describes 26 rooms across two floors. Its photographs show several bedroom styles, including twin rooms and four-poster beds, so use the room description for your chosen rate rather than assuming every room matches the main photograph. The hotel also has a garden and terrace. This is a place to use as a base for exploring the island, with somewhere to sit down at the end of the day.

Food, parking and everyday facilities

ZenHotels lists a bar, restaurant, breakfast, free Wi-Fi and free parking. Check whether breakfast is included in the room rate you select; a hotel offering breakfast does not mean every booking includes it. Laundry and luggage storage are also listed. For a short seaside break, being able to leave the car at the hotel and return for a meal is part of the appeal.

Accessibility and arrival

The listing reports wheelchair access to the restaurant and accessibility features, but also says there is no lift. Ask for confirmation of a suitable bedroom, bathroom and step-free route before booking if stairs would be a problem. The published check-in window is 15:00–23:00, with check-out by 10:30. Arrange a late arrival directly. The partner lists pets as not allowed; discuss assistance-dog arrangements with the hotel.

Making a Hayling break of it

Beachlands and Funland are the natural seaside pairing. Leave time for the beach or a quieter island walk rather than treating every day as a drive to Portsmouth. The wider attractions below are additional trips: Portsmouth and Chichester are not the same location as the hotel. The booking options give you a way to compare the actual room, board basis, cancellation terms and final total for your dates.

Clarence Pier Amusements

Clarence Pier brings seaside amusements to Southsea, with arcades, fairground rides and other attractions. It is a Portsmouth outing rather than a venue on Hayling Island.

Seasonal rides and year-round planning

The operator now states that the fairground rides have closed for the 2026 season and will return in 2027. Arcades and other activities have their own opening arrangements. Check the current opening page before travelling; a summer ride photograph does not mean the ride is operating today.

Paying for your visit

Ride tokens and wristbands are different products from arcade play. Read the current prices, height restrictions and operating dates before buying. Plan an arcade budget separately and check which attractions a wristband covers.

Around Southsea

You can combine the pier area with a seafront walk or another Southsea attraction, but allow time for the journey back to Hayling. Check access, toilets and food arrangements for your group using the venue’s current visitor information.

Weald & Downland Living Museum

Weald & Downland Living Museum is near Singleton, north of Chichester. It is a wider heritage day out for visitors staying several days around Hayling and the South Coast.

A different sort of day out

The museum centres on historic buildings and rural life. Allow time to explore the site rather than treating it as a short indoor museum stop. The setting makes it a useful change from beach and arcade days.

Tickets and access

Use the museum’s current visitor information for opening dates, admission and the programme. Check access to individual historic buildings and outdoor routes, along with mobility support, toilets and food options. Older buildings and an outdoor site need more specific planning than a blanket wheelchair-friendly label.

Where it fits

This is a mainland journey beyond Chichester. Plan it as a substantial outing with suitable footwear and clothing for the weather. The museum website supplies the current booking and visitor details.

Vue Portsmouth (Gunwharf Quays)

Vue Portsmouth is at Gunwharf Quays, making it an option for a film and a meal during a Portsmouth day or evening. It is a separate mainland trip from Hayling Island.

Choose your screening

The venue has 14 screens, and Vue’s current listings include its EPIC format. Compare the film, format, seat and time on the live programme; prices and available screenings change. Book against the Portsmouth venue rather than a general cinema search.

Access and planning

Check Vue’s venue-access and accessible-screening information for the session you want, including wheelchair spaces, subtitled, audio-described and autism-friendly options where scheduled. Leave time to travel to Gunwharf Quays, park or walk from public transport, and find the correct screen.

Make an evening of it

Gunwharf Quays has food and drink options around the cinema. Choose the film time first, then plan a meal around it. The showtimes button goes to the cinema’s own live listings.

fields.guideContent:
Fort Nelson

Fort Nelson is a restored Victorian fort on Portsdown Hill, with artillery, ramparts and tunnels overlooking Portsmouth Harbour. Entry is free, making it a useful heritage stop on a wider coastal trip.

What is here

Royal Armouries describes more than 19 acres to explore, with large artillery pieces and changing exhibitions. The setting is part of the visit: allow time for the fort as well as the displays. There is an on-site café and family activity programme.

Opening and practical details

The published autumn term-time pattern is Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00–17:00, with daily opening during the stated school-holiday period. Check the live calendar for your date. Advance booking is recommended at busy times. Entry is free, but parking is chargeable for non-members and some special tours cost extra.

Visit planning

Children aged 15 and under must be accompanied by a responsible adult. Check the access information before choosing a tunnel or rampart route. This is on the mainland, so include the road journey in a Hayling itinerary rather than describing it as a walk from the island.

Blue Reef Aquarium Portsmouth

Blue Reef Aquarium is on Southsea’s seafront, offering an indoor marine-life visit during a wider Portsmouth day. It can be useful when a Hayling beach plan needs a change of weather.

Plan the visit

Use the aquarium’s current visitor page for the day’s opening time, last admission and ticket options. Allow time to look around at your group’s pace rather than booking it between two tight appointments. Seasonal activities can add to the visit, but check what is running on your date.

Practical arrangements

Check the official accessibility information for step-free routes and any mobility requirements. Confirm parking and toilet arrangements before travelling, especially if this is your main wet-weather option. Family ticket combinations and online prices should be checked against the ages of your group.

A mainland outing

The aquarium is in Southsea, not on Hayling Island. It can pair with a seafront walk or the D-Day Story nearby, with the travel time included in your plans. The official website button provides current visitor and ticket details.

fields.guideContent:
Portsmouth Historic Dockyard

Portsmouth Historic Dockyard is a substantial day out in its own right. Ships, museums and naval stories give you far more to explore than a quick stop between other attractions.

What to see

The partner ticket lists major attractions including HMS Victory, HMS Warrior, HMS M.33, the Mary Rose Museum and Royal Navy museums. Check the precise ticket coverage and any restoration restrictions for your date. Some included sites are separate from the main waterfront entrance, so plan how you will reach them.

Tickets and revisiting

The advertised ticket offers repeat access for a year. Read the product terms to confirm activation, included sites and any exclusions. This can be useful if you are staying nearby and would prefer to spread the museums over more than one visit rather than rush them all in an afternoon.

Facilities and access

The partner lists cafés, toilets, accessible toilets, shops and parking nearby. Historic ships have uneven surfaces and confined areas, so consult the access information for the individual attractions. Assistance dogs are accepted; ordinary pets are not. Check companion-ticket arrangements when booking.

Make room for the day

The entrance is at Victory Gate in Portsmouth, close to Portsmouth Harbour station. It is a mainland outing from Hayling Island. Plan your return travel and leave time to sit down for food, especially with children or anyone who needs regular breaks.

fields.guideContent:
Mill Rythe Coastal Village

Mill Rythe Coastal Village is Away Resorts’ holiday park on Hayling Island. Choose a holiday home or lodge and make time for the pool, family facilities and trips around the island.

Staying at Mill Rythe

The operator offers holiday homes and lodges, with different layouts and accommodation grades. Some options include hot tubs, but they are not a feature of every booking. Check the number of bedrooms, sleeping arrangements, pet policy and parking for the exact unit. An accessible Westwood accommodation option is advertised on the ways-to-stay page.

Food, swimming and family facilities

Away Resorts lists the Missing Squirrel and Green Room for food and drink, an indoor pool, soft play, an adventure playground, a sports court and a seasonal outdoor splash area. These give families something to do around the park between trips out. Entertainment is seasonal, so check the timetable for your dates rather than assuming a summer programme runs throughout the year.

Activities and practical arrangements

The park also lists a fishing lake and bike hire. Fishing requires the operator’s pass and an appropriate rod licence. Bookable activities and entertainment are managed through the Away Resorts app. Ask the park about any activity fees, pool booking, visiting guests and access to facilities if you are not staying there.

Holiday park and arcade are different listings

The holiday accommodation, restaurant, pool and entertainment are the focus here. If your visit is specifically for amusement machines, use the separate arcade page and check current public access with the operator. A holiday-park booking does not establish a particular machine line-up.

Explore the island from your stay

Funland and the seafront provide a contrasting outing, while the Donkey Sanctuary needs checking against its advertised visiting sessions. Portsmouth and Chichester attractions are wider trips across the mainland. Use the park booking option to check accommodation availability and terms for your dates.

Chichester Lakeside Holiday Park

Chichester Lakeside is a Park Holidays UK site on the mainland outside Chichester. It offers a countryside-and-lakes setting for a longer coastal break, with Hayling Island as a separate day trip.

The location

The operator describes a setting around ten fishing lakes and countryside outside the historic city. West Wittering and Bognor Regis are among the coastal trips it highlights. That makes this a wider West Sussex base, rather than accommodation on Hayling Island itself.

Choose your accommodation

Check the live park booking page for the accommodation available on your dates, the number of bedrooms and the maximum occupancy. Pet-friendly and pet-free accommodation can have different conditions. Confirm any fishing arrangements, leisure access and seasonal programme directly against your chosen stay.

Access and planning

Before booking, ask about the route from your holiday home to the facilities, parking, steps into the accommodation and bathroom layout. Lakeside surroundings do not establish that every unit has the same access. Leave time for the road journey if you are travelling to Hayling’s seafront or booking a timed activity elsewhere.

Booking your stay

The park’s official holiday page is linked here for current accommodation and facility details. Compare the full stay cost and cancellation conditions before reserving.

fields.guideContent:
Langstone Quays Resort

Langstone Quays is a waterside resort at the northern end of Hayling Island. It works particularly well for visitors who want a hotel break with leisure time as well as trips out to the island and Portsmouth.

The resort and bedrooms

The partner offer is for two people in a Classic or Superior Double Room. It describes en-suite bathrooms, Wi-Fi, television and tea and coffee facilities. The gallery shows the exterior, pool, bedrooms, restaurant and waterside setting. Choose the room category during booking rather than assuming an upgrade is included.

What the current partner package includes

The Things To Do page currently advertises an overnight stay for two with breakfast, an arrival glass of wine, leisure access, free on-site parking and 13:00 checkout. It offers afternoon tea or a £35-per-person dining-credit upgrade. Selected travel dates run until 30 April 2027. These are package terms: check the selected option and final booking page, especially when comparing against a room-only rate.

Leisure, food and access

The offer lists an 18-metre pool, jacuzzi, sauna, steam facilities and gym. Spa treatments can be booked separately. The Waterside Restaurant, lounge bar and terrace give you options for staying at the resort for the evening. Contact the hotel about suitable rooms and access to the particular leisure facilities you want to use; the offer alone does not establish every accessibility detail.

A sensible base for exploring

Allow a separate outing for the south-coast beach and Funland, and another for Portsmouth if the Dockyard or Gunwharf Quays is on your list. The hotel’s harbour setting is part of the reason to stay here, so avoid filling every hour with driving. Use the offer button below for available dates and exact inclusions.

fields.guideContent:
Funland Amusement Park

Funland is Hayling Island’s seafront amusement park, with rides, arcades and other family activities. It is one of the island’s natural choices for a traditional seaside day.

Choose the parts of the park you want

Rides, arcade play, soft play and other attractions can have different prices and operating arrangements. Check the current Funland programme rather than assuming one ticket includes every activity. The separate arcade guide covers that part of the venue in more detail.

A practical seaside visit

Use the official directions page to plan the journey and parking. Check ride height restrictions, access needs and seasonal opening before setting off. Allow time for food, toilets and a break from the games, particularly with younger children.

Make a day of Hayling

The seafront location makes it easy to build a day around the park and beach. Hotels and holiday parks below are places to stay, with their own booking terms. An amusement-park visit does not require treating every nearby offer as another stop to fit in.
